Clothes & getting dressed

take off verb

clothes

also undress, get undressed

classical

exuō, exuere, exuī, exūtum

verb, third conjugation

Examples

  • Hanc vestem exue.

    Take this garment off.composed

  • Puer, calceīs, pilleō, paenulā dētractīs, in lectum suum positus est

    The boy, his shoes, cap and coat taken off, was put into his own bedFābula VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

Other words

  • dētrahō, dētrahere — take off (clothes, shoes)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 118

See also put on, get dressed.

SourcesLewis & Short: exuo · Lewis & Short: detraho

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 118, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater: Fābulae Latīnae ad vītam cotīdiānam I–VII, as revised on 29 October 2026. Examples marked “Fābula” quote those texts word for word.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
